# SOM

Built the way the spec asks: from how many institutions can we realistically acquire. Not from a share of a market we have not yet shown exists.

## The plan we are rejecting

`todo.md` PHASE 7 proposes *5 institutions in year 1, 15 in year 2, 40-50 in year 3*. That is rejected, in writing, for three reasons:

1. The year-3 figure implies roughly 50 paying institutions. That requires a sales team which does not exist and a contract value nobody has agreed to pay.
2. It implies a conversion rate well above the 2-20% prior we are working from, and conversion is precisely the quantity no interview has measured.
3. It was never derived from anything. A plan that starts from a target and works backwards is not a plan; it is a preference with a table around it.

## What capacity actually supports

Reachable accounts by year 3, from the seeded Monte Carlo (seed 20261019, 50,000 trials):

- Reachable accounts (yr 3): 150-300
- Conversion rate: 0.02-0.06
- Binding constraint: **conversion**, r = 0.65

The binding limit is conversion, and that is the point worth making to an investor: the constraint is not how many institutions exist, and it is not what they can pay. It is whether we can close them, and we have not yet asked a single one.

## Capacity-built projection, both scenarios

Logos are the modelled p25-p75 from the Monte Carlo. The envelope is the analytic outer bound (product of the reachable and conversion endpoints). The quantile of a product is not the product of the quantiles, so the two differ, and both are shown rather than reconciled.

| Year | Ramp | Logos A (p25-p75) | Envelope A | ARR A (cr) | Logos B | ARR B (cr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10% | 3-5 | 0-12 | 0.0-0.1 | 3-5 | 0.3-0.5 |
| 2 | 32% | 10-16 | 1-38 | 0.1-0.2 | 10-16 | 1.0-1.7 |
| 3 | 60% | 19-31 | 2-72 | 0.2-0.4 | 19-31 | 1.9-3.2 |
| 4 | 80% | 25-41 | 2-96 | 0.3-0.5 | 25-41 | 2.6-4.2 |
| 5 | 100% | 31-52 | 3-120 | 0.4-0.6 | 31-52 | 3.2-5.3 |

Ramp is 10/32/60/80/100% of year-3 capacity. These are capacity projections, not commitments.

## The number to underwrite

**Scenario A, year 3: 19-31 paying institutions, Rs 0.2-0.4 crore ARR.**

At Scenario B the same capacity yields Rs 1.9-3.2 crore - and that number is a function of a price nobody has been asked about, not of any additional customer work.

## The state layer sits outside this number

Segment G9 (34 State Startup Nodal Departments) is sized separately in State_SOTP.md and is **not** added to the SOM above. It is a different buyer, a different deal shape and a different timeline.
